name: From Invention to Patent
description:
Research results are important sources for new products and services in the era of Open Innovation for business
and industry. But how can research results be protected and commercialized?

A practice-oriented introduction to intellectual property rights, with a special focus on university inventions:
In addition to patents, other relevant areas of intellectual property (IP) — such as design protection, domain and trademark protection, and utility models — are thoroughly covered by experts in each field.

The course explores the path from invention to obtaining the respective IP right, its legal enforcement in court, and the economic
exploitation of the IP right, particularly in the context of university spin-offs. Students will then deepen their understanding of patenting opportunities in their specific technical disciplines through practical case studies, working in separate groups based on their fields of study.
